reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an instructional guide to creating a YouTube channel on a phone, including ordinary setup, account verification, and feature-eligibility steps. The frames show Google sign-in, channel creation, and YouTube Studio settings rather than a request for payment, unrelated credentials, or financial participation. The promotion of free resources, a waitlist, and referral-linked material is framed as video-marketing education with possible affiliate compensation disclosed.

citations.quote: I'll show you exactly how to create a YouTube channel with your phone step by step
in order to have a YouTube channel, you will also need to have a Google account
you will need to verify your account
check out our free resource which is linked on screen

opening.argument: Judge the offer as a promise paired with an action, not just as channel-setup advice. The description tells viewers they can learn strategies to "10X" their traffic and immediately asks them to get a free ranking guide. The closing pitch again connects better search placement to a linked resource. Calling the first step free does not resolve what viewers are being drawn into; the material does not establish that obtaining the guide delivers the advertised result. That promise-to-click linkage is the concern.

citations.quote: Learn the 3 most powerful tools & ranking strategies to 10X your traffic on YouTube! Grab the FREE YouTube Ranking Guide
check out our free resource which is linked on screen

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accurately identifies real setup instructions, but those instructions do not answer the concern about the linked offer. Google sign-in and YouTube account verification are part of the demonstration; they do not substantiate the separate claim that a free guide can help deliver dramatically greater traffic. An affiliate disclosure addresses possible compensation, not whether the promoted result is supported.

citations.quote: Learn the 3 most powerful tools & ranking strategies to 10X your traffic on YouTube! Grab the FREE YouTube Ranking Guide
if you click one of the links in this video or description and make a purchase we may receive a small commission or other compensation

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted language offers a free educational guide about ranking strategies; it does not promise that merely clicking will award traffic, money, or an asset. The video gives concrete channel-setup instructions, including how to reach YouTube's own verification page. Nothing cited shows a deceptive claim flow or a required payment to obtain a reward.

citations.quote: Grab the FREE YouTube Ranking Guide
it's gonna take us off to another website here, which is youtube.com forward slash verify to verify our account

opening.argument: Look at the signals together: a large "10X" traffic claim, a free guide at an external link, and a separate program pitched around generating leads "on autopilot" and scaling a business. The description also invites viewers onto that program's waitlist. None of those phrases proves a guaranteed outcome, but their combination makes the free resource look like the entry point to a business-growth solicitation. The tutorial's useful details should not prevent scrutiny of that pitch.

citations.quote: Learn the 3 most powerful tools & ranking strategies to 10X your traffic on YouTube! Grab the FREE YouTube Ranking Guide
Join the Primal Video Accelerator waitlist: https://primalvideo.com/accelerator?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_content=bs2odsqBBMM
Learn how to build an audience, generate new leads on autopilot and SCALE your business with video step-by-step

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's sign-in and settings examples establish that the tutorial has genuine instructional content. They do not erase the adjacent claims about multiplied traffic and automated leads. Nor does describing a resource as free establish what the waitlist leads to or validate the business-growth language. The issue is the cumulative promotional message, not whether the on-screen YouTube controls are real.

citations.quote: 10X your traffic on YouTube! Grab the FREE YouTube Ranking Guide
generate new leads on autopilot and SCALE your business

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are promotional phrases for training about video marketing, not evidence of an easy payout or a hidden acquisition flow. The description identifies the Accelerator as a program about building an audience with video and openly discloses possible referral compensation. The cited material shows a free guide and a waitlist, but no promised cash reward, mandatory purchase, or deceptive verification step.

citations.quote: Learn how to build an audience, generate new leads on autopilot and SCALE your business with video step-by-step in our fast-track Primal Video Accelerator program!
Wherever possible we use referral links, which means if you click one of the links in this video or description and make a purchase we may receive a small commission or other compensation.

opening.argument: The channel walkthrough is also a route into the presenter's own offerings. Early on, viewers are directed to the description links; after the setup demonstration, the presenter directs them to a free resource tied to getting content into top search positions. The description extends that path to a ranking guide and an Accelerator waitlist. So the question is not whether the instructions work. It is whether the educational format lends credibility to an external, results-oriented solicitation whose advertised gains are not demonstrated by creating a channel.

citations.quote: all the links to everything we mention in this video you'll find linked in the description box below
the tools and techniques that we use to get our content showing up in the top of spots on both Google and YouTube
Join the Primal Video Accelerator waitlist:

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the promotion as incidental because the frames show ordinary YouTube screens. But a real demonstration can still build trust for an offer made afterward. The closing invitation asks viewers to move from channel setup to the presenter's linked resource for search-ranking techniques. The demonstrated settings do not independently establish that this additional offer produces the results used to attract viewers.

citations.quote: then check out our free resource which is linked on screen, taking you through our keyword research process
get our content showing up in the top of spots on both Google and YouTube

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion does not make an instructional video a scam. The presenter walks through creating a channel, choosing settings, and verifying it through YouTube; the linked resource concerns the related topic of keyword research. The cited pitch describes techniques viewers can learn, not a reward awarded for clicking. The defense need not prove that every marketing claim succeeds to distinguish this tutorial from a deceptive acquisition scheme.
